body.en: A deformed body develops an internal restoring force. The restoring force per unit area is called *stress*, σ = F/A, measured in N m⁻² or pascal (Pa). Stretching or squeezing along the length gives longitudinal (tensile or compressive) stress; a force parallel to a face gives shearing stress; a uniform force from all sides gives hydraulic stress.
body.kn: ವಿರೂಪಗೊಂಡ ವಸ್ತುವಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಪುನಃಸ್ಥಾಪಕ ಬಲ ಉಂಟಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಏಕಮಾನ ವಿಸ್ತೀರ್ಣದ ಮೇಲಿನ ಪುನಃಸ್ಥಾಪಕ ಬಲವೇ ಪ್ರತಿಬಲ, σ = F/A. ಇದರ ಏಕಮಾನ ಪ್ಯಾಸ್ಕಲ್. ನೀಳ ಪ್ರತಿಬಲ, ಶಿಯರ್ ಪ್ರತಿಬಲ ಮತ್ತು ದ್ರವಸ್ಥಿತಿ (ಹೈಡ್ರಾಲಿಕ್) ಪ್ರತಿಬಲ ಎಂಬ ಮೂರು ವಿಧಗಳಿವೆ.

title.en: Stress and strain on the board

say.en: Hang a wire of length L and cross-section A from a rigid support, and pull it with a force F.
Inside the wire, a restoring force appears. Restoring force per unit area is the stress, measured in pascal.
The wire stretches by ΔL. The fractional change in length is the longitudinal strain. It is a ratio, so it has no unit.
Worked numbers: F = 200 newton on a wire of area 2 square millimetre, 2 metre long, stretching by 1 millimetre.
There are three kinds of stress and strain: longitudinal, shearing, and volume, or hydraulic.

narration.en: Stress is the restoring force per unit area, F/A; strain is the fractional change in shape or size. Pull and you get tensile (longitudinal) strain, push sideways on the top face and you get shear strain, squeeze from all sides and you get volume strain. The block is aluminium; the change is drawn 100 times larger.
narration.kn: ಪ್ರತಿಬಲ (ಸ್ಟ್ರೆಸ್) ಪ್ರತಿ ಏಕಮಾನ ವಿಸ್ತೀರ್ಣದ ಪುನಃಸ್ಥಾಪಕ ಬಲ, F/A; ವಿಕೃತಿ (ಸ್ಟ್ರೇನ್) ಆಕಾರ ಅಥವಾ ಗಾತ್ರದ ಭಾಗಶಃ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ. ಎಳೆದರೆ ಉದ್ದದ ವಿಕೃತಿ, ಮೇಲ್ಮುಖವನ್ನು ಪಕ್ಕಕ್ಕೆ ತಳ್ಳಿದರೆ ಕತ್ತರಿ ವಿಕೃತಿ, ಎಲ್ಲ ಕಡೆಯಿಂದ ಒತ್ತಿದರೆ ಗಾತ್ರ ವಿಕೃತಿ. ಬ್ಲಾಕ್ ಅಲ್ಯೂಮಿನಿಯಂ; ಬದಲಾವಣೆಯನ್ನು 100 ಪಟ್ಟು ದೊಡ್ಡದಾಗಿ ಚಿತ್ರಿಸಲಾಗಿದೆ.

body.en: *Strain* is the fractional change in size or shape. Longitudinal strain is ΔL/L, shearing strain is Δx/L = tan θ ≈ θ, and volume strain is ΔV/V. Strain is a ratio, so it has no unit and no dimensions.

problem.en: A 2 m long wire of cross-section 2 mm² stretches by 0.5 mm under a load of 100 N. Find the stress and the strain.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A 2 m long wire of cross-section 2 mm² stretches by 0.5 mm under a load of 100 N. Find the stress and the strain.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A 2 metres long wire of cross-section 2 square millimetres stretches by 0.5 millimetres under a load of 100 newtons. Find the stress and the strain.
A equals 2 square millimetres equals 2 times 10 to the power minus 6 square metres.
Stress equals F over A equals 100 / (2 times 10 to the power minus 6) equals 5 times 10 to the power 7 newtons m to the power minus 2.
Strain equals delta L over L equals 0.5 times 10 to the power minus 3 divided by 2 equals 2.5 times 10 to the power minus 4.
So the answer is Stress equals 5 times 10 to the power 7 pascals; strain equals 2.5 times 10 to the power minus 4.
